model.rationale: Hawaii's urban Honolulu district leans heavily Democratic, and incumbent Ed Case is running again with over $1 million raised against minimally funded challengers. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Case underperforming the district's lean, or unusual top-two dynamics in Hawaii's nonpartisan primary system, would be the main signals to watch.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st district, covering urban Honolulu, is a strongly Democratic seat with a 13-point partisan lean. Ed Case, the incumbent since 2019, is seeking another term and has raised about $1.1 million, holding roughly $600,000 on hand. His Republican challenger, Adriel Lam, reports no fundraising figures, and minor-party and independent candidates are also on the ballot.

No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the incumbent's financial advantage. Prediction markets give the Democratic side roughly a 96% chance of holding the seat, consistent with the district's history of comfortable Democratic margins.
